pairs.statement: The claim must be brought before the social section within six months of the delivery of the non-conciliation record, or the right to bring it is forfeited.

Cases are listed before the sections by the nature of the dispute; in courts without sections the civil section hears every dispute except social cases; a case listed before the wrong section is passed to the proper section.
The social section of the court hears this claim.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT establishes jurisdiction over specified employment, training and apprenticeship disputes, but does not identify this claim as one of them.

pairs.statement: Before a claim in which always, a prior step must have been taken.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT describes internal dispute procedures and permits notifying the labour inspector after their exhaustion. It does not establish an unconditional prerequisite before every court claim.

pairs.statement: A claim before the social section is brought by a statement of claim.
The labour inspector passes the referral to the conciliation office and summons the parties within three days of being notified.
Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is a matter of public order, which the court raises of its own motion at any stage.
When the parties do not agree, the office draws up a record of non-conciliation.
The plaintiff is notified of the striking-out decision within eight days of the decision.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The supplied paragraph does not identify the decision as a striking-out decision.

pairs.statement: When the duly summoned defendant misses consecutive conciliation meetings as the text sets out, the office draws up a record of non-conciliation for non-attendance.
When worker is public servant is yes, the case leaves the ordinary courts (outsideCatalogue).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT excludes specified public-service disputes from conciliation offices and assigns administrative jurisdiction according to the public parties involved. It does not establish that civil-servant status alone removes a case from the ordinary courts or places it outsideCatalogue.

pairs.statement: Judgments on the application or interpretation of an agreement made before the conciliation office, or on the payment of wages and allowances for the most recent months the text names, are provisionally enforceable by law.
When the last day of the period is not, wholly or partly, a working day, the period runs to the next working day.
The claim is brought before the court for the place where the employment relationship is performed or for the defendant's residence.

Before a claim in which nonconciliation record is no or nonconciliation record is unknown or (nonconciliation record is yes and nonconciliation record delivered on is before the petition's date), a conciliation attempt before the labour conciliation office must have taken place, except when: Conciliation is optional when the defendant resides outside the national territory; Conciliation is optional when the employer is bankrupt or under judicial settlement; Disputes of civil servants and agents under the statute of public institutions and administrations are outside the conciliation offices.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not use the record's absence, unknown status, or delivery strictly before the petition date as conditions for requiring prior conciliation. It states a general requirement for individual labour disputes, with the stated exceptions.

pairs.statement: The first hearing is set within fifteen days at most of the date the claim is filed.
Individual disputes to which civil servants and agents governed by the statute of public institutions and administrations are party fall outside the conciliation offices.
The request to lift the forfeiture goes to the president of the court before which the dispute is brought, who rules by an order on petition open to no remedy.
The periods of this Code are counted in full: neither the day of notification or service nor the day the period ends is counted.
When public body party is yes, the case leaves the ordinary courts (administrativeCourt).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT identifies particular public entities and excepts disputes assigned to other jurisdictions. It does not establish that participation by any unspecified public body automatically removes a case from the ordinary courts.

pairs.statement: The time limit is 6 months, running from the date of nonconciliation record delivered on; it is a forfeiture period, counted by the method excludeFirstAndLastDay; it applies when nonconciliation record is yes and (forfeiture lifted by order is unknown or forfeiture lifted by order is no) and (forfeiture force majeure invoked is unknown or forfeiture force majeure invoked is no).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the yes/no/unknown conditions concerning a lifting order or invocation of force majeure. It does not equate absence of an invocation with absence of force majeure; its exception concerns actual force majeure or disruption of the justice service.

pairs.statement: The conciliation office may strike the matter out when the plaintiff or the plaintiff's representative fails to attend without a serious and lawful excuse.
The expiry of a forfeiture period is a ground for a plea of inadmissibility, without examining the merits.

An individual labour dispute is a disagreement between a salaried worker and an employer on the performance of their employment relationship that internal settlement within the employer has not resolved.
The petition to the court is accompanied by a copy of the record of non-conciliation issued by the conciliation office.
A salaried worker performs manual or intellectual work for pay, within an organisation and on behalf of another person, the employer.
The record of conciliation is proof unless it is challenged as forged.
The parties carry out the conciliation agreement on the terms and within the time they set, failing which within thirty days of the agreement.
After the internal procedures are exhausted, the worker may refer the matter to the labour inspector.
The petition is registered only once the fees set by law are paid, unless the law provides otherwise.
The president of the social section orders immediate execution under a penalty payment.
When the employment contract ended or was suspended because of a work accident or an occupational disease, the court for the plaintiff's domicile has jurisdiction.
This prior step is not required when: Disputes of civil servants and agents under the statute of public institutions and administrations are outside the conciliation offices.
Failure to respect a period this Code sets for exercising a right forfeits the right, except in case of force majeure or events affecting the normal working of the justice service.
The courts hearing social matters decide individual disputes arising from the performance, suspension or termination of an employment relationship.
The court decides at first and last instance claims to annul disciplinary sanctions taken without the required procedure and claims for work certificates and pay slips.
A copy of that record is handed to the plaintiff at the meeting.
The court for the place where the employment contract was made or performed, or for the defendant's domicile, has territorial jurisdiction.
Collective agreements may set internal procedures for handling individual disputes within the employer.

The time limit is 6 months, running from the date of nonconciliation record delivered on; it is a forfeiture period, counted by the method excludeFirstAndLastDay; it applies when nonconciliation record is yes and (forfeiture lifted by order is unknown or forfeiture lifted by order is no) and forfeiture force majeure invoked is known and forfeiture force majeure invoked is yes.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not specify application based on a mere invocation of force majeure or yes/no/unknown information about a lifting order. It expressly excepts actual force majeure or events affecting the justice service; invocation alone is not identified with that exception.

pairs.statement: When a conciliation agreement is not carried out, the president of the court hearing social matters, seised by petition, orders the immediate execution of the conciliation record with a daily penalty payment.
When the parties agree on all or part of the dispute, the office draws up a record of conciliation.
When conciliation fails, the party with an interest brings the claim before the court hearing social matters.
The judge raises a plea of inadmissibility of his own motion when it is a matter of public order.
Every individual labour dispute must go through a conciliation attempt before the conciliation office before any court action is brought.
Legal aid is granted as of right to every worker or trainee whose pay is below twice the guaranteed minimum wage.
The local jurisdiction of the conciliation offices is set by regulation.
Non-working days falling inside the period are counted.

Civil servants and contract agents of the public bodies and administrations of the State, wilayas and communes, staff of public administrative bodies, and other groups, are governed by special provisions.
Immediate execution may be sought from the president of the social section when a party refuses to carry out a conciliation agreement.
Failing such procedures, the worker refers the matter to the direct superior and then to management or the employer, each of whom must reply within a set time.
Conciliation is optional when the defendant resides outside the national territory, or when the employer is bankrupt or under judicial settlement.
The labour inspectorate is seised by a written request or by the plaintiff in person, in which case the inspector records the plaintiff's statements.
The social section has exclusive jurisdiction over social security and retirement disputes, listed as an item separate from employment contracts.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT establishes exclusive jurisdiction over social security and retirement disputes as item 6, but does not show an employment-contract item against which the asserted separation can be checked.

pairs.statement: The administrative courts have general jurisdiction over administrative disputes, except the disputes given to other courts.
This prior step is not required when: Conciliation is optional when the employer is bankrupt or under judicial settlement.
Non-working days, in this Code, are the official public holidays and the weekly rest days under the texts in force.
The plea of lack of territorial jurisdiction must be raised before any defence on the merits or plea of inadmissibility.

The administrative courts hear at first instance the cases to which the State, a wilaya, a commune, a public administrative body, a national public body or a national professional organisation is a party.
Additional requests that follow from the original request are admissible at every stage of the claim, even if they were not put to the conciliation attempt.
This prior step is not required when: Conciliation is optional when the defendant resides outside the national territory.
The social section sits, on pain of nullity, as a presiding judge with assessors as labour legislation provides.
At least eight days must run between the summons and the day fixed for the parties to appear.
When the defendant or the defendant's representative fails to attend, a new summons is issued for a conciliation meeting held within eight days at most.
It may be brought before the court for the plaintiff's residence when the suspension or end of the employment relationship results from a work accident or an occupational disease.
The record of conciliation may not contain terms contrary to the texts in force.
The social section has exclusive jurisdiction over the proof, performance, suspension and termination of employment contracts.
